requirements.requirement: Every command run through sudo on node1 is logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the invoking user and timestamp.
requirements.summary: A valid global sudoers drop-in configures the dedicated logfile and year-bearing timestamps. Direct probes before and after reboot produced entries containing timestamps, invoking user, target user, and command; the earlier entry persisted across reboot.

requirements.requirement: Sudo command entries are kept out of the general system log.
requirements.summary: The effective global sudo defaults include !syslog. Uniquely tagged sudo commands had zero matches in both /var/log/messages and the system journal before and after reboot.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 globally logs sudo commands with user and timestamp to the dedicated file while excluding them from general logs. Configuration, prior log data, and behavior survived a fully evidenced reboot.
limitations: Functional command probes used root as the invoking user; coverage for all users is supported by the global Defaults configuration rather than a direct non-root probe.
The fixed after-executor platform observation timed out, although direct post-reboot checks and the remaining lifecycle observations showed node recovery and health.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the sudoers drop-in was the required implementation (cmd-f66e0e9825164961); test sudo invocations were bounded functional evidence (cmd-1c8862cc99e04b46, cmd-bf6a58b8ae774439); and the reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol (cmd-affdbc23ee264276). The restart evidence is complete and independently corroborated by changed lifecycle boot identities. Afterward there were no failed services, unexpected listeners, package-health damage, or abandoned temporary files.
